PHONEMES:
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

phonemes start with ampersand (&) unless in phoneme mode

truvoice -> arpa/dectalk-like

A		ey
a		ae
B		b
b		uw
C		ch
c		uh_r		// tour
D		d
d		hv			// voiced HH
E		iy
e		eh
F		f
f		aw
G		g
g		ao_r		// four
H		hh
I		ay
i		ih
J		jh
j		lx			// postvocalic light L
K		k
k		eh_r		// hair
L		l
l		el			// syllabic L
M		m
N		n
n		en			// syllabic N
O		ow
o		aa
P		p
q		tq			// glottalized T (like in "button")
R		r
r		aa_r		// hard
S		s
s		sh
T		t
t		dx			// alveolar flap (like in "butter")
U		y_uw		// "huge" and "donahue"
u		uh
V		v
v		ah
W		w
w		ao
X		th
x		dh
Y		y
y		oy
Z		z
z		zh
~		ng
3		er			// could be "axr" too, but I don't think TruVoice can differentiate unstressed/stressed "er"
4		ih_r		// "hear"
5		ay_r		// "fire"
@		ax			// unstressed schwa
|		ix			// unstressed fronted schwa
1		'			// primary stress
2		"			// secondary stress



FOUND ESCAPE SEQUENCE COMMANDS:
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\x1B[ - escape sequence start (always starts with escape character \x1B and end with [ )
{d}   - number


\x1B[{d}V		# voice

\x1B[{d}a		# amplitude (volume. higher value is lower)
	range: 0 -> 16

\x1B[{d}r		# speech rate
	range: 50 -> 250

\x1B[{d}p		# pitch
	range: 50 -> 400 hz

\x1B[{d}X		# context mode (for reading special text like email messages)

\x1B[{d}c		# voice/character mode (0 - normal, 1 - whisper, 2 - monotone)

\x1B[{d}I		# text/phoneme mode (0 - text, 1 - phoneme)

\x1B[{d}f		# fast/skim read mode. this skips some words to speed up reading.

		0    = speaks all text ('this is a test. how do I sound?')
		1    = speaks just nouns? ('test... sound?')
		2    = speaks just the last noun? ('sound?')
		3... = no speech for the example sentence.

\x1B[{d}P		# speaks out words individually without regular prosody.

		0    = word read
		1    = regular prosody

\x1B[{d}s		# initiates a silence/pause with number as duration in milliseconds

\x1B[{d}t does something. It tests phonemes. only used by the developers for debugging the synthesizer :D


UNKNOWNS TO INVESTIGATE FURTHER:
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When \x1B[5A is used, it speaks really fast.

\x1B[{d}g does something. It first produces a schwa sound then speaks text. Duration is based on the given number?

\x1B[{d}v does something. it messes with the speech rate? low number is slow, and high number (max might be 20) is fast

\x1B[{d}x does something. no speech comes out tho (0 - 255 is the number range)
